# temps_node_resources (Resource)

Capacity Temps keeps for itself on a node and whether the scheduler enforces reservations there. Destroying the resource leaves the settings as they are.

Import with `<node_id>`.

Required API key permissions: `settings:read`, `settings:write`.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# Node 0 is the control plane.
resource "temps_node_resources" "control_plane" {
  node_id                    = 0
  resource_policy            = "best_effort"
  system_reserved_cpu_millis = 1000
  system_reserved_memory_mb  = 2048
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `node_id` (Number) ID of the node; `0` is the control plane.

### Optional

- `resource_policy` (String) Whether reservations count against the node's capacity. One of `best_effort`, `enforced`.
- `system_reserved_cpu_millis` (Number) CPU kept for Temps, in thousandths of a core.
- `system_reserved_memory_mb` (Number) Memory kept for Temps, in MiB.

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) Import ID, `<node_id>`.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# <node_id>
terraform import temps_node_resources.control_plane 0
```
